dull ache.

ASSESSMENT & PLAN: ___ with ongoing alcohol abuse but no known 
liver disease transferred from ___ to ___ for 
monitoring of hematemesis and black bowel movements, found to 
have esophageal varices and ___ Tear, requiring 3 
bands for hemostasis, and new diagnosis of cirrhosis.

# Acute Gastrointestinal Bleed: hematemesis and dark stools were 
concerning for upper GI bleed.

Endoscopy done at ___ were 
only revealing for nonbleeding questionable gastric and 
esophageal varices.

No intervention done at ___ as unable to 
clearly see source of bleed.
He was subsequently transferred to

___ ICU for further evaluation and management of 
hematemesis/melena.
He was initially continued on octreotide,
PPI BID.
GI was consulted on arrival to ___.

He was intubated 
for airway protection and underwent EGD by GI on ___.

Results 
of the EGD showed one cord of grade III, two cords of grade II 
and one cord of grade I esophageal varices, as well as a likely

___ Tear (thought to be the causal lesion of the 
hematemesis and melena).

These lesions required a total of three 
bands.

He was subsequently continued on ceftriaxone for SBP 
prophylaxis in setting of bleed, octreotide.

H/H remained stable 
and he was transferred to the ___ Medical floor.
On the

Medicine floor, the ceftriaxone was transitioned to 
ciprfofloxacin and octreotide gtt was transitioned to nadolol.

H/H at the 
time of discharge was 9.9/30.7.

# Alcoholic Cirrhosis: New diagnosis, as patient had esophageal 
varices noted on EGD and right upper quadrant ultrasound with 
doppler which showed "coarsened and heterogeneous hepatic 
architecture...patent hepatic vasculature...splenomegaly."

Likely alcoholic given his history of alcohol abuse, but work-up 
for alternative sources was carried out including hepatitis 
panel, AFP, LFTs, Iron tests for hemochromatosis (ferritin),
AMA, anti smooth muscle.

Hepatitis Panel was notable for 
negative HBsAg, HBsAb, HBcAb, HCV Ab Anti-mitochondrial
Antibody, Anti-Smooth Muscle antibody, ___.
AFP was 3.3.

RUQ-US 
did not reveal concerning solid liver lesions (there were two 
hepatic cysts noted).

Alpha-1-antitrypsin was also obtained and 
was normal at 160.
Iron studies revealed a serum iron 229, TIBC
363, Ferritin 21, Transferrin 279.

As part of initial transplant 
work-up patient underwent an echocardiogram which showed 
sub-optimal image quality, but mild symmetric left ventricular 
hypertrophy, overall left ventricular systolic function of 70%, 
normal right ventricular chamber size and free wall motion, 
moderate aortic valve stenosis (valve area=1.1 cm2), mild mitral 
regurgitation.
Given these findings, he will require a repeat

Given new diagnosis of cirrhosis, he will need to be vaccinated 
against Hepatitis A and Hepatitis B in the future.

ALT 57, AST 85.
Albumin

Given that

1 mg PO daily.
